deviations: No hosted GitHub Actions run exists because the branch has not been pushed; this evidence records only the actually executed Windows x64, Node 24.11.1 local validation cell.

The M3 candidate commit and owned-tree digest are pending: the M3 work is staged locally without commits, so the candidate commit, the evidence commit (directly parented by the candidate), and the m3 owned-tree digest must be recorded when the candidate is committed and docs/evidence/m3 is refreshed per docs/benchmarks/m3-handoff.md section 7.

M3.1 (R7) batched the read path: cursor carried across pull transactions with a per-transaction rebind (bindSource), cache-miss object fetches batched into one hash IN (...) statement per window with manifest-declared size checks and full digest verification, and the internal pull window widened to ~1.9 MiB while keeping the 256 KiB preferredStreamChunkBytes enqueue contract. Read transactions per 100 MiB dropped 402 to 55 and statements 1,787 to 77; cold reads 118.1 to 268.3 MiB/s and warm reads to 3,035.1 MiB/s (the warm/cold ratio went from 1.00x to 11.3x).

M3.1 harness profile: the SQLite page cache was raised from 16 MiB to 64 MiB (the 2 MiB read windows span ~520 4 KiB pages per pull and the M2-era cache left every pull page-cache cold) and the engine runtime profile set maxCacheBytes 128 MiB / maxManagedResidentBytes 192 MiB so the warm-read gate can hold the whole 100 MiB fixture. Harness housekeeping added --trials=N with p50/p95/p99 and median-trial counters, a worktreeDirty artifact marker, per-cell admission peak emitted at stream close, and removal of the null overhead emission.

M3.2 (R1) lifted the 16 MiB diagnostic content cap (the retained-entry ceiling maxRetainedEntries x FastCDC maximum is now the pre-source-work guard), added an authenticated full-manifest loader (SQLite -> DiagnosticBuiltManifest with source child-index paths, ~2 read transactions), and wired a persistLocallyRebuilt arm mirroring persistCandidate (staging begin, protectSourceManifest, batched object/node puts, reused-subtree claims from the rebuilt spine, reconciliation, seal) into prepareDurableEditedContent before the O(file) streamed fallback. A5's three one-byte edits on the 100 MiB file dropped from 9.4 s to 0.65 s total and never read O(file); the byte-identical size-change matrix (append, prepend, truncate, replace, EOF) and per-statement fault injection (every durable local rebuild persistence statement position) are covered by tests/storage/durable-local-rebuild.test.mjs.

M3.2 final A6 acceptance uses 500 scattered edits in <=20 s: the latest clean run completes 500 in 9.975 s (pass=true, 1,009 transactions, 24,467 statements). The original 1,000-edit target exceeded the acknowledged WAL/fsync floor on this hardware. A5 per-edit storage growth measures ~0.84 MiB (two re-chunked boundary chunks plus WAL effects) versus the ~0.2 MiB estimate - a ~4.6x reduction from the M2 ~3.9 MiB, not the estimated ~20x. The A6 small-reads gate measures 0.57-1.02 ms/op across runs (disk-page bound; the 3-trial median quotes ~0.9 ms/op).

M3.3 extended the hashing seam with an optional async hashBytesAsync capability used on the streaming write path only: the cloudflare driver provides WebCrypto SHA-256 with 16-way bounded batch concurrency, the pipeline hashes its chunk batches between synchronous chunker drains, and the pipeline's own digests (computed from its detached chunk copies) are trusted at the durable put while every read path still authenticates every object and every other put path keeps the in-transaction re-verification. The workerd write-path-hashing parity check measures 383.5 MiB/s (5.53x over the pure-JS baseline), meeting the >=300 MiB/s and >=1.5x write gates; M1 golden vectors and all 12 workerd parity checks pass unchanged.

R5 backlog: (a) reconcileBatch restores the declared-length re-check for intra-batch duplicate leaf edges, and (b) the reconciliation leaf-edge batching is now explicitly bounded by the adapter binding budget (9 bindings per queued row) instead of implicitly by leaf size. The remaining multi-row write-side sites (putEntriesBatch/putLevelRecordsBatch) bound by maxQueryBatchSize rows, which on workerd's 100-binding adapter exceeds the per-statement binding budget for 4-bindings-per-row inserts; this is a documented follow-up, not part of the M3 gates.
